questions.question: Explain the concept of assertiveness and discuss why assertiveness training is important, especially for women.
questions.solution_html:
• Concept of Assertiveness
  • • Many people have a hard time being assertive; however, this problem is more common
  • among females because they are socialized to be more submissive than males—to “be
  • nice.” Generally, people tend to associate assertiveness with direct person-to-person
  • social interactions.
  • • Assertiveness is also important in indirect exchanges as well. Learning to be assertive in
  • email or text messages or on social networking sites is also important.
  • • Assertiveness involves acting in one’s own best interests by expressing one’s thoughts
  • and feelings directly and honestly.
  • • Essentially, assertiveness involves standing up for your rights when someone else is
  • about to infringe on them.
  • • Submissive communication is deferential, as it involves giving in to others on points of
  • possible contention. Submissive people often let others take advantage of them.
  • • Typically, their biggest problem is that they cannot say no to unreasonable requests.
  • • A common example is the college student who can’t tell her roommate not to borrow her
  • clothes.
  • • Submissive people also have difficulty voicing disagreement with others and making
  • requests themselves. In traditional trait terminology, they are timid.
  • • They appear to lie in excessive concern about gaining the social approval of others.
  • • Aggressive communication focuses on saying and getting what one wants at the
  • expense of others’ feelings and rights. With assertive behavior, however, one strives to
  • respect others’ rights and defend one’s own.
  • • The problem in real life is that assertive and aggressive behaviors may overlap.
  • Assertiveness training is especially popular among women. Men, too, find assertiveness
  • training helpful, both because some have been socialized to be passive and because others
  • want to learn to be less aggressive and more assertive.

questions.question: Describe the components of vocal variety.
questions.solution_html:
• There are certain important constituents of a good voice channel. These are
  • • Pronunciation and Articulation - Pronunciation refers to your ability to utter the words
  • in the same way as is considered standard..
  • • Articulation refers to coherence of the words and phrases in a talk. When a person
  • is articulate, the message would be easier to understand for the audience. Articulation
  • stems from proper pronunciation but is more than mere pronunciation.
  • • Emphasis –When you are speaking, not everyone in the audience tunes in to your
  • speech the way you think they should.
  • • Pace – Pace refers to how fast you speak.
  • In general, in many cases, higher the pace of speech, the more persuasive it is.
  • Higher pace gives an aura of confidence for the speaker but also gives less opportunity
  • for the audience to intervene.
  • • Pitch- Pitch refers to how shrill your voice is – the baseline frequency of your
  • voice.
  • The pitch of your voice is dictated by the thickness and length of your vocal chords.
  • Each of our voices has some limits within which we can ‘stretch’ them.
  • Too much of stretching will be physically painful for the speaker and may be jarring for
  • the listener.
  • • Volume –Volume refers to the loudness with which you speak.
  • Some people habitually speak so loud that you wish you had a remote control button for
  • controlling their volume!
  • At the other extreme are people who talk so softly that they can barely be heard even
  • when you sit close to them. To be effective you need to strike a balance.
  • Volume goes in tandem with other parameters like speed, pitch, and articulation.
  • • Pause- A good presentation should not be a continuous outpouring of words
  • without any gaps.
  • Periodic pauses during a presentation are essential. These enable you to recover your
  • breath and also enable the audience to reflect on what you have said.
questions.final_answer: breath and also enable the audience to reflect on what you have said

questions.question: Explain the concept of assertiveness and discuss why assertiveness training is important, especially for women.
questions.solution_html:
• Concept of Assertiveness
  • • Many people have a hard time being assertive; however, this problem is more common
  • among females because they are socialized to be more submissive than males—to “be
  • nice.” Generally, people tend to associate assertiveness with direct person-to-person
  • social interactions.
  • • Assertiveness is also important in indirect exchanges as well. Learning to be assertive in
  • email or text messages or on social networking sites is also important.
  • • Assertiveness involves acting in one’s own best interests by expressing one’s thoughts
  • and feelings directly and honestly.
  • • Essentially, assertiveness involves standing up for your rights when someone else is
  • about to infringe on them.
  • • Submissive communication is deferential, as it involves giving in to others on points of
  • possible contention. Submissive people often let others take advantage of them.
  • • Typically, their biggest problem is that they cannot say no to unreasonable requests.
  • • A common example is the college student who can’t tell her roommate not to borrow her
  • clothes.
  • • Submissive people also have difficulty voicing disagreement with others and making
  • requests themselves. In traditional trait terminology, they are timid.
  • • They appear to lie in excessive concern about gaining the social approval of others.
  • • Aggressive communication focuses on saying and getting what one wants at the
  • expense of others’ feelings and rights. With assertive behavior, however, one strives to
  • respect others’ rights and defend one’s own.
  • • The problem in real life is that assertive and aggressive behaviors may overlap.
  • Assertiveness training is especially popular among women. Men, too, find assertiveness
  • training helpful, both because some have been socialized to be passive and because others
  • want to learn to be less aggressive and more assertive.
questions.final_answer: want to learn to be less aggressive and more assertive
